title: Expert-level Leaf Cell Layout Generation via Preference-Optimized LLM
one_liner: Generate circuit layout scripts that approach or exceed expert designs by learning what good layouts look like and then preferring scripts whose outputs match those high-quality designs.
lead: This paper targets leaf cell layout generation for integrated circuits. The challenge is unusual: expert layouts exist, but the scripts that produced them do not. That means the training target is visible in final form while the action sequence that created it is missing. GenLeaf bridges that gap with three steps: learn a representation that scores layout similarity in performance-aware ways, use search to create candidate script-layout pairs, and then train and refine a language model to prefer scripts whose resulting layouts resemble strong expert designs.

problem.h2: Why layout generation is hard without expert scripts
paras: Leaf cell layouts matter because they are reused many times inside larger circuit designs. Small improvements in these cells can therefore affect the power, speed, and area of a much larger chip.

The data problem is severe. Experts can provide final layouts, but they often do not provide the exact scripts that generated those layouts. A model that learns only from final physical shape lacks the action trace that would show how to rebuild the design.

callout.html: Use the expert layout as the target signal and create missing script supervision through search, because the final design still tells you which generated scripts are worth preferring.

panels.viz_args: strong final leaf cell designs are available
panels.caption: The target quality is visible in finished layouts, but the script history is missing.

panels.title: 2. Learn to score similarity
panels.caption: A learned scorer estimates which generated layouts are close to strong expert layouts in quality-relevant ways.

panels.title: 3. Search for script-layout pairs
panels.viz_args: propose scripts and keep those that create strong layouts
panels.caption: Search provides missing training pairs because high-scoring outputs point back to useful scripts.

panels.caption: The final model writes scripts that produce layouts with strong power, speed, and area tradeoffs.

steps.text: The system first learns a representation that can compare one layout with another in a way that tracks design quality, because raw visual similarity alone is not enough.
A search procedure proposes scripts and keeps the ones that create high-scoring layouts, so expert layouts can indirectly supervise the script space.
Accepted search results become training pairs because they link layout quality back to concrete script choices.
The model learns to produce scripts that recreate strong layout patterns seen in the derived dataset.
The model is further tuned to prefer script outputs whose final layouts score better, so it is pushed toward expert-level design quality.

paras: The paper changes leaf cell layout generation from direct imitation with missing supervision into a two-stage process that first reconstructs useful script data and then teaches the model to prefer the scripts that yield stronger layouts because final layout quality provides a usable training signal.
object.object: the script that generates a leaf cell layout

hidden.name: quality of a script as measured by the layout it will produce
paras: The key hidden quantity is the quality of a candidate script before you run it to completion. Two scripts may look equally plausible as text, yet one creates a compact, high-performing layout while the other wastes area or harms timing.

GenLeaf estimates that hidden script quality through the generated layout. The learned scorer and the preference stage matter because they let the model connect text choices with final design consequences, even when expert scripts are unavailable.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark the hidden properties that determine whether a script is truly good once it becomes a physical layout.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is how good a script will be after it becomes a layout, because script text should be judged by the circuit layout it causes.
The method converts final-layout quality into supervision over script choices, then sharpens that supervision through preference optimization.

mechanism.h2: Why derived script data plus preference learning helps
paras: The search-created dataset solves the missing-supervision problem. Expert layouts alone show the destination, but not the route. Search fills in routes by exploring script candidates and keeping the ones that lead to strong final layouts. This works because the layout scorer turns final physical quality into a signal that can rank script choices.

Preference optimization then improves beyond plain supervised fitting because two scripts may both generate valid layouts while only one saves area or improves timing. A preference signal pushes the model toward the better script because the model is rewarded for choosing text that leads to stronger design outcomes, not merely for reproducing a plausible script string.

stages.s: rank scripts by final layout outcome

math.h2: Judge a script by the layout it yields
math.words: A compact summary is to score a script by the quality of the generated layout relative to a strong expert target, then prefer the script that yields the better final design.
symbols: overall value of one candidate layout script
the layout produced when script s is executed
how good the produced layout is on power, speed, and area related criteria
how far the produced layout is from the desired expert-level layout pattern

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Script A produces a compact layout with strong timing, so layout quality is 9.
Its mismatch from the expert target is 2, so the total score is 7.
Script B produces a valid but larger layout with weaker timing, so layout quality is 6.
Its mismatch is also 2, so the total score is 4.
Script A is preferred because it reaches a stronger final physical design.

math.note: The paper uses a learned scorer, search, and preference tuning rather than this exact line, but the line captures the point: the worth of a script is determined by the layout it creates.

charts.title: Direct generation without strong outcome feedback
charts.note: Direct generation struggles because the model lacks script-level supervision tied to final physical design quality.

charts.title: GenLeaf
charts.note: The paper reports strong power, speed, and area results because search reconstructs useful supervision and preference learning pushes the model toward higher-quality scripts.

items.b: The learned scorer may value the wrong layout traits.
items.html: If the scorer overvalues superficial similarity, search may keep scripts that look close to expert layouts but miss the deeper physical qualities that matter.

items.b: Search may explore too narrow a script region.
items.html: If candidate generation stays near one local pattern, the derived dataset may miss better script families because those alternatives were never tried.

items.b: Preference tuning depends on reliable pairwise comparisons.
items.html: If the system cannot clearly tell which of two layouts is better, the preference signal becomes noisy because later script choices no longer receive a consistent ranking signal.
The method is strongest when the layout scorer aligns with real design quality, because then every retained script teaches the model something useful about better final layouts.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small layout domain with a simulator that turns scripts into final layouts and returns power, speed, and area related measurements. Hide the expert scripts but keep several expert final layouts. Compare three systems: direct script generation, generation trained on search-created pairs, and generation further refined by preference optimization.

The demo should show that the latter two systems move closer to expert-level outcomes because they gain supervision from produced layouts rather than from missing script traces alone. It should also show whether preference tuning improves beyond plain fitting by selecting between valid scripts that differ in final physical quality.
demo.closing: A convincing demo must prove that script generation improves when final layout quality is turned into supervision, because expert layouts reveal what good scripts should achieve even when the scripts themselves are missing.
